notes.note: Gen 10 is an undated genealogy of nations (the Table of Nations); by the skill's rule undated genealogies are framing. Verses left out of any event: 10:1-7, 10:13-17, 10:20-24, 10:26-32 (name lists, family and territorial summaries). 10:1 and 10:32 say only that the sons were born and the nations spread 'after the flood'; no event could be dated from them beyond what the Peleg and dispersal events already carry.

The narrative-like items (Nimrod, Asshur's cities, Peleg, the Canaanite spread) carry no stated date. Their placement is by relation to the Flood anchor and to each other, all MACRO_ERA with wide margins; the order Nimrod, Asshur, Peleg's days, Canaanite scattering is the text's order, not a proven sequence (10:11 'from that land' puts Asshur's building after Nimrod's kingdom; the Targum Pseudo-Jonathan says Asshur left to avoid the counsel of the generation of the division, i.e. the Babel episode, which is Gen 11 and may fall in Peleg's days).

No causal links written: there is no divine or prophetic speech in the chapter, so nothing to check for fulfilment; a possible link from Noah's words 'Canaan be a servant' (9:25) concerns later chapters. The sequence between the Nimrod and Asshur events is recorded in the timeline, and 'because' is not stated in the text.
